title: UatEvidence
description: Contract for tasks/builds/<slug>/uat-evidence.json — the machine-readable verdict a fresh-context acceptance run produces (codex-brief §8.6, plan A6/A7/A8). Producer: the fresh executor (Codex CLI/Desktop, or Claude-headless under advisory enforcement). Consumer: scripts/uat/validate-uat-evidence.mjs, which populates status.json ONLY from validated evidence, never the reverse. STRUCTURAL FAIL-CLOSED NOTE: every object here is additionalProperties:false, so a break-glass field such as `uat_enforcement_override` is rejected by shape alone — the validator ALSO deep-scans for that exact key (plan A2/A3: no override ships; attempted override fields are rejected, not carried dormant). JSON Schema validates one document's shape; the cross-document invariants (blind ⊆ final-required ⊆ executed, risk-baseline superset, artifact hash recomputation, plan-digest identity, realpath containment, secret scan) are enforced by the validator, which is the system of record.

run_id.description: Namespaces every resource this run touched (scratch dir, DB name, temp dirs, browser profile, artifact names) — plan A10. Two concurrent runs never share a run_id.

verdict.description: Exactly the four brief verdicts. No 'pass with caveats'. Fail-closed: the validator never translates incomplete/fail into pass/proceed.

applicability.description: Recorded distinctly from verdict and enforcement (plan round-3 finding 5). non-applicable REQUIRES verdict=proceed and an applicability_reason; proceed appears for genuine non-applicability ONLY.

applicability_reason.description: Required when applicability=non-applicable. Free-text justification, SHA-bound by the surrounding candidate identity.

enforcement.description: The SINGLE downstream control (plan round-4 finding 3). Derived from the final risk inventory + rollout mode by the acceptance phase and recorded here; refusal rows and label transitions consume this, never the raw rollout mode. Monotonic advisory->blocking; never de-escalates.

late_discovered_risk.description: Present when a risk discovered DURING execution escalated enforcement and the frozen plan could not cover its mandatory families (plan §10 late-risk rule). Each entry names the tag and the missing families; its presence with verdict=incomplete is the honest outcome.

candidate.description: The APPLICATION candidate under test (plan A7). Distinct from `harness` — the thing that judged it.

head_sha.description: Full 40-hex candidate SHA. An abbreviated SHA is a rejection for verdict=pass.

runtime_tree_clean.description: false with any non-allowed dirty path is a rejection for pass.

submodule_shas.description: path -> 40-hex SHA for every materialised submodule. An intentionally excluded submodule is recorded as an input limitation elsewhere, never silently omitted.

allowed_dirty_paths.description: Dirty paths permitted without invalidating cleanliness — limited to UAT evidence/scratch roots.

harness.description: The UAT harness that produced the verdict (plan A7). Records every semantic input's identity so a pass under an unrecorded overlay is impossible; `harness_manifest_sha256` is the completeness boundary (round-3 finding 7).

planner.description: The blind-planning identity, separate from execution (plan round-3 finding 9). The blind runtime config is hash-bound here; a fresh thread is asserted (round-4 finding 1).

fresh_thread.description: Asserts the planner thread/context id was newly created — no resume, no prior thread.

blind_runtime_config_sha256.description: Hash of the effective hermetic runtime configuration (isolated CODEX_HOME, web_search off, memories off, env allowlist policy). Bound into evidence per A6.

sanitised_env_var_names.description: NAMES/policy only of the environment variables the clean allowlist removed or retained — never values (plan A6, credential non-readability).

execution.description: The scenario-execution identity, separate from the planner. Desktop may execute a CLI-produced frozen plan (blindness already spent in planning).

plan_digests.description: The two-sided plan-digest handoff (plan round-4 finding 6). The validator requires expected == executed (and == recomputed from the plan file when supplied) — a frozen plan cannot be swapped between validation and execution.

expected_plan_sha256.description: Computed by the coordinator over the final uat-plan.json before dispatch.

executed_plan_sha256.description: Recomputed by the executor over the plan file before its first scenario.

blind_scenario_ids.description: The frozen blind scenario id set (bound by plan_digests.blind_plan_sha256). The set invariant is checked against this: every id here must appear in scenarios[] as required=true and be executed — deletion, downgrade, or non-execution of a blind scenario is a rejection (plan A6).

risk_baseline.description: The independently-derived minimum risk set produced BEFORE blind execution (plan A8) and hash-bound into the blind input manifest. The tester may add risks but never remove a baseline one; the validator enforces final ⊇ start ⊇ baseline.

risk_inventory_at_execution_start.description: Immutable snapshot frozen at execution start, hash-bound to the executed plan (plan round-6 finding 3). Plan completeness at execution start is checked against THIS.

risk_inventory_final.description: Monotonic superset carrying late-discovered risks. Enforcement and audit metrics derive from this.

capabilities.description: Capability inventory with availability evidence (brief §8.2). pass with a required-but-unavailable capability is a rejection; 'browser unavailable' is never a browser pass.

augmentation_started_at.description: MUST be strictly after blind_plan_frozen_at (validator rejects <=) — augmentation cannot precede the freeze.

secrets_redacted.description: A claim, not proof — the validator independently secret-scans textual evidence. secrets_redacted:true with a seeded credential in a captured artifact is a rejection (plan A8).

uat_advisories.description: Shadow/advisory surfacing channel (plan round-3 finding 8). A fail/incomplete under enforcement=advisory writes here — NEVER the framework's machine-blocking field in status.json.

executor_class.description: plan A2. claude-headless is lower-assurance evidence and can never satisfy enforcement=blocking.

risks.description: The set of risk tags. Order-independent; the validator compares as sets.

sha256.description: Canonical (RFC 8785) digest of the `risks` set — integrity binding.

origin.description: blind scenarios came from the sealed first pass and can never be removed or downgraded; augmentation may only ADD coverage.

families.description: The scenario-family keys (from risk-to-scenario-policy.json) this scenario covers. Drives the coverage cross-check.

oracle.description: The pass/fail decision rule for this scenario.

anti_vacuity.description: STRUCTURED proof the intended branch ran (plan A8) — not free text. At least one field must be present and meaningful for an applicable scenario; a 200/empty/zero is not evidence for a path that requires stored data.

evidence.description: Evidence artifacts as {path, sha256, bytes, media_type, redaction_status} (plan A8). The validator recomputes sha256 + bytes against the real file and secret-scans textual media.

digest.description: RFC 8785 canonical digest of THIS scenario object with its own `digest` field excluded.
